content:
Working on the last remaining sorry in BKLNW.lean (thm_1b_table). Currently have 132/430 cells passing (exact literal constants, no sorry).

Ran into a design question regarding table_11_margin: since the margin is baked into the type, most cells become unprovable against the literal printed values from the paper. Should we target the exact printed values or keep the margin-adjusted version?

Per §13 disclosure: code is AI-assisted. Full code/details here: https://github.com/lsmeng/pnt-table15-evidence

Could someone add thm_1b_table to the project board?

One should apply the margin in order to make the table entries verifiable (and able to absorb roundoff errors etc.).

I've opened PNT#1761 for this. Heads up: I am in the process of building a new IEANTN site to migrate all the code over, but legacy work here at the PNT+ site should be portable over when the site is complete.
